why: The check topology and timeout ownership affect CI reliability, but the runtime semantics themselves already have a bounded owner
evidence: Bead haxe_ocaml-tqv34 requires preserved null-safety, measured latency, and owned cleanup
result: Applied high for the task; Oracle was not needed because sampling exposed a local, testable compiler performance boundary

decision: Isolate the slow null-safety owner before changing the gate
why: Moving or narrowing the compilation boundary without measurement could hide a real package-wide null-safety failure
evidence: Exact-type runs completed OcamlRuntimeUseModel in 0.37 seconds and OcamlFinalRuntimeUseAuthority in 0.29 seconds, while OcamlRuntimeUseAuthority exceeded a 10-second timeout
result: The slow behavior belongs to one class rather than package size, repeated compilation, or classpath growth

decision: Replace the closed Boolean name chain with a string switch
why: Haxe 4.3.7 null-safety was expanding the 42 equality branches rather than executing the fixture
evidence: A macOS process sample spent almost all sampled time in NullSafety.process_condition, traverse, and is_suitable; the long equality chain was the unique large condition in the exact slow class
result: The same 42 names remain reserved without combinatorial condition analysis

decision: Preserve and strengthen the independent semantic oracle
why: A faster compiler check must not silently alter which private names are rejected
evidence: RuntimeUseAuthorityFixture now lists all 42 reserved names independently and also checks three similar names that must remain allowed
result: The switch is locked to both positive and negative behavior

decision: Keep package-wide null-safety and add a per-phase deadline
why: The source fix makes the faithful boundary fast, so narrowing null-safety would reduce evidence without a performance benefit
evidence: All three runner phases retain nullSafety("reflaxe.ocaml"); cold phase times were 1077, 237, and 912 milliseconds under a 30-second budget
result: The original semantic and null-safety claims remain intact, with phase-specific failure output

decision: Terminate only the runner-owned compiler tree
why: A caller timeout must not kill another repository job or leave a compiler child behind
evidence: The runner creates a POSIX process group or uses Windows taskkill /T; its fixture launches a parent and grandchild that resist TERM and proves both are gone after KILL
result: Timeout cleanup is bounded, process-tree scoped, and independently exercised
